$comment: The source of sf-chat-window's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.9, vocabulary 1.1.5. Moved from simai/ui-chat components/src/smart/chat-window (smart.manifest.json 0.3.1, ui-chat 07bc988) by the D31 move, step 6 (owner yes 2026-10-27), with files-view.js, port.js, chat-core's larena.js words and smart.css, and the staff page's layout of the window's nodes; written by hand on the shape of sf-chat-interlocutor, sf-chat-composer and sf-chat-message (steps 3-5), since migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs takes only the pinned 66. x-decisions says how each point was decided.

capabilities.x-markup: the port's capabilities the host offers (assistant, people, files, edit, delete, feedback, proposals, conversation-create, conversation-manage, interlocutors, read) and the window's own (x-archive-view, x-conversations-paging, x-conversations-search, x-conversation-pin, x-early-upload, x-my-files, x-brief), space-separated; a connected port's capabilities count as well. What is not offered is not shown. The property also takes a list (0.3).
capabilities.summary: The port capabilities the host offers, space-separated (assistant, people, files, edit, delete, feedback, proposals, conversation-create, conversation-manage, interlocutors, read), and the window extensions (x-archive-view, x-conversations-paging, x-conversations-search, x-conversation-pin, x-early-upload, x-my-files, x-brief). What is not declared is not offered, and its intent is answered unavailable without an event. The property also takes an array.

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16); it places the shell the element builds once as plain DOM.

skeleton.$comment: No late data: a server prints the window with the host's data as its JSON island (the conversations, the open conversation and its messages), and the static markup is the whole window as drawn -- the shell with the parts' own markup (the list, the log with its sf-chat-message nodes, the header, the field). The port, handed later, brings no first-paint data; what it answers is what a person asks for afterwards (§5.4).

accessibility.x-keys: The window is the page's main landmark (landmark main) or a region (section) with an off-screen heading of the conversation's title (heading-level). The conversations are sf-thread-list (a navigation list), the conversation sf-message-log (a log that says each new answer once: the stage while it waits, «Ответ готов» before it, footnote marks not read), the field sf-chat-composer. The search above the list is a search landmark; Enter asks at once, Escape clears it first and then belongs to the page; what was found is said politely. A passing line above the field (role=status) says what was just done and offers its undo («Вернуть»); an error is role=alert with «Повторить». The focus never falls to the page: an archived row gives it to «Вернуть», a pinned or restored row keeps it, an answer that comes back gives it to the field, «Мои файлы» take it on their heading and give it back to the field; in «Мои файлы» Escape closes a delete question first, then the view, and a delete question takes the focus on «Отмена». The queue (1.1.0): a question asked while an answer is awaited waits over the field as a card in a list named «Отправлю после ответа», with «Изменить» and «Убрать» (and «Отправить» when held), each described by its question; that it was queued, and why a queue is held, is said politely. The search in the conversation (1.1.0) is a search landmark over the log, opened by open-find or Ctrl/Cmd+F with the focus inside the window: Enter goes to the earlier match, Shift+Enter to the later one, as up and down do; «N из M» and «Ничего не найдено» are said politely after a pause; Escape clears the query first, then closes the search and returns the focus to what opened it. Matches are painted with the CSS Custom Highlight API (Mark and Highlight in forced colours), the message's text is not touched.

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-chat-window for the shim (core/js/aliases.js, standard §16 item 20). The 0.3 window raised each port intent as chat-port:<name> and each window capability as chat-window:<name>, with {request_id, ...payload}; 1.0 raises one event per verb, sf-chat-window-<verb> {request-id, intent, kind, payload} (vocabulary 1.1.5 §5, §5.1), so every row is split, sent only when the detail's intent is the one the old name stood for (when, since a verb carries several old names), and the element adapter (sfAliasAdapters) makes its 0.3 detail. sf-chat-window-answer became the fact settled.

The carried field is requestId (camelCase, as the registry says); the detail keeps "request-id" beside it and settle takes either, until 2026-12-01 with the dated event names.

queue (1.1.0): the queue is the window's, not the composer's: what a conversation is, when an answer is over and how it ended are the window's data (messages, status, wait), and a queue belongs to its conversation. The composer only lets a message of text out while busy (its setting queue, 1.1.0), and the window keeps it per conversation key (as the drafts) and draws its cards above the field, where the passing line already is. When the field lets go of busy, the last turn decides: answered (completed, partial; without the assistant capability, a question taken) sends the first card, which waits for its own answer before the next; failed, limit, refused, withheld, a stopped or unfinished wait, a send not taken, or a conversation left before its answer hold the queue with a quiet line, and each card can be sent («Отправить», which lets the rest go on after its answer) or taken away. Stop stops the wait only. A queued question goes out as an ordinary message.send (no new intent, no new port word); one that did not go is tried again under its first client_key (message.retry). A message with files is not queued (its chips are the host's upload state). Off with no-queue. Nothing is stored.

find (1.1.0): the search in the conversation reads only the drawn messages (the question's bubble, the answer's body, a person's message; not buttons, sources or off-screen words) and asks the host nothing; the port 1.0.0 has no search of a conversation and a server search would be the port's 1.1.0. The Framework offers no find helper (its highlight component colours code), so the marks are the CSS Custom Highlight API, which touches no node of a sanitized message; without it the message holding the current match is outlined. The current match starts at the last one, nearest where the reader is, and Enter goes up, as in a chat's history. open-find and close-find are the actions (as open-files and close-files), toggle {kind: find, open} the event and data-find-open the host state, so a page's header button can show itself pressed. Ctrl/Cmd+F is taken only while the focus is inside the window (as the inline editor's Mod+K), so the page's own find stays the browser's elsewhere.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-chat-window for a whole chat: conversations, the open conversation and the field, on a host that implements simai.chat-port 1.0.0 (Mirai24's assistant, simai.chat).
do_not: Do not fetch from the element: hand it a port (connect-port) or answer its events with settle
Do not answer an intent both through a port and through settle
Do not decide what a person may do from who wrote a message; give can_edit and can_delete
Do not build a second list of conversations beside it; the window's sf-thread-list is the one
Do not keep a queue of your own for messages sent while an answer is awaited; the window queues and sends them after the answer (no-queue turns it off)
ai_guidance.minimal_example: <sf-chat-window capabilities="assistant feedback proposals conversation-create conversation-manage"></sf-chat-window> with element.connectPort({port: 'simai.chat-port', version: '1.0.0', capabilities: [], raise: (intent, payload) => host.answer(intent, payload)}) and element.setData({me, conversations, conversation: null, messages: []})
owner_commands: node scripts/run-first-paint.mjs gate <free output> <package output> chat-window

accessibility.focus: The parts keep their own keyboard (the list's roving focus, the field's Enter). After a new conversation or another interlocutor the focus goes to the field; when the last awaited answer of the conversation ends it returns there without scrolling. When what held the focus is gone (an archived row), the way back above the field takes it, never the page. A passing line leaves only when no pointer or focus is on it and hands the focus back to the field. The queue's «Изменить» puts the question back in the field and the focus there; «Убрать» moves the focus to the card in its place, else to the field. The search in the conversation takes the focus when opened and gives it back to what opened it when closed.

The queue: a question sent while an answer is awaited waits above the field as a card («Отправлю после ответа», «Изменить», «Убрать») and goes as an ordinary message.send after a successful answer, one at a time; an answer that ended otherwise holds the queue for «Отправить» by hand. Per conversation, on this page only. The setting no-queue turns it off. No new intent and no change for a host.

The search in the open conversation: the actions open-find {query} and close-find {focus}, Ctrl/Cmd+F inside the window, the event toggle {kind: find, open} and the host state data-find-open. It searches the loaded messages only and asks the host nothing.

applyData.summary: Set several of the port's data at once (and the extension data); unknown keys are ignored. Each datum is also a property of its own name. Kept from 0.3; the action set-data is its manifest form.

schema.description: Any of the port data (me, conversations, conversation, messages, history, feed_state, limits, interlocutors, notice) and the extension data (conversation_list, composer_files, my_files).

revoked.description: Access is gone: the component clears the feed, the draft and anything unsent.

id.description: null only for a send not yet stored (then local is required).

kind.description: person: written by a person (the reader or another); assistant: an answer of an AI assistant.

body.description: Plain text; shown as text, line breaks kept.

html.description: assistant only: server HTML, sanitized again by the component.

created_at.description: Omitted when the host does not know it; the component never invents a time.

proposal.description: capability proposals: a change applied only on the confirmed command.

key.description: Local opaque key of a file not yet stored (a failed upload); never sent to download or delete.

is_deleted.description: A tombstone: no body, no files.

command.description: A message sent for a button (a proposal's command): {kind: confirm|cancel, code}.

body.description: An edit's typed text; kept on failure and conflict.
